stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up
stories.summary: Which teams are in the best position heading into Decision Day? All this and more in the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday and another weekend of action is in the books. With Decision Day coming up next week, it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings to see which teams are in a good or bad spot to qualify for the MLS Cup playoffs.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While seeking history on a rainy night in Tennessee, Nashville fell behind by two goals, had multiple goals called off, but battled back to force two own goals and clinch a 3-2 win against Red Bull New York with stoppage-time headed goal from Sam Surridge. The Supporters' Shield winners are level with Miami's points record, but could break it with just a point from their final game.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 2

Miami reclaimed second place in the Eastern Conference with a second-half rally against the Revs to win 2-1, ignited by the guy still leading the Golden Boot race: Lionel Messi. After a headed assist to Germán Berterame to level the score, Messi scored his 26th goal of the year after finagling past multiple defenders then sending a low left-footed strike past Matt Turner.

3. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 4

The Revs' four-game win streak came to a halt against the Herons, as Messi proved the difference maker once more assisting and scoring in a come-from-behind win for Miami. With that, New England drops to third place in the Eastern Conference. Silver lining? Dániel Gazdag is now on a two-game scoring streak.

4. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 3

STL had the firepower in the attacking third to come away with all three points against San Diego. But thanks in part to Pablo Sisniega's six saves and Anders Dreyer's moment of quality, they went home with a 1-0 defeat instead. The playoffs were already locked up but home-field advantage isn't as they head into the final weekend.

5. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

After going scoreless in six games, Robert Lewandowski came off the bench to make the difference in Colorado, providing the go-ahead goal 10 minutes after subbing on, then setting up Puso Dithejane for the 4-2 win.

6. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 7

The Whitecaps showed their quality in a comprehensive 5-1 dismantling of Seattle, highlighted by a Brian White brace that started in the 56th minute. After a 4-1 win over San Diego in midweek and 29th-place Montréal up next, the Western Conference's first-place side have got some momentum ahead of the postseason.

7. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

After drawing Nashville 0-0 in the midweek, Philly's 1-0 loss to Cincinnati is their second in three games. They'll be in the postseason, but they may have a tough matchup when it comes.

8. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 9

With the Golden Boot technically still in reach, Petar Musa (who scored 22 goals this season) missed his first penalty in six this season in the 97th minute. Stefan Cleveland's late-game save kept the Toros from three points in a 1-1 draw as they head into the final weekend looking to secure second place in the Western Conference.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

After losing 3-1 to Minnesota, LAFC are winless in three (two draws) ahead of a Decision Day battle with the Sounders. With their playoff place secure, they're competing for a better finish in the standings, but will fall short of their top-three finish in the Western Conference in the last four seasons.

10. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

Kristijan Kahlina, whose save percentage (75.9%) is second only to first-place Nashville's Brian Schwake (77.7%), stopped eight against Orlando in a match that ended 4-0 in Charlotte's favor, despite both teams firing off the same number of shots (and nearly the same on target, though Charlotte had higher quality opportunities).

11. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 11

After losing 4-0 to mid-table side Charlotte, Orlando picked up their first defeat in six games but still clinched their playoff spot based on other results. They're in the final wild card spot ahead of a final test against the Revs.

12. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

The Quakes took 17 minutes to score twice against RSL, and that was enough to secure three points in a 2-1 win. That's their first win in six (four draws, one loss) as they look to secure their third-place spot in the Western Conference.

13. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 10

In a 5-1 loss to Vancouver, Jordan Morris' brief light of life in the second half was overshadowed by the Whitecaps' rapid response in a match characterized by goalkeeper Andy Thomas looking painfully skyward for help from the scoreline. After losing to Houston in midweek, the Sounders have three defeats and no wins from their last five games. They play LAFC on the final day while sitting one place short of the wild card spots.

14. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 14

Morgan Whittaker scored from close range to mark his third goal in three games and take an early 1-0 lead against Chicago. But at the end of a goal-heavy matchup, Lewandowski scored and assisted off the bench to help see the Fire to a 4-2 win. The Rapids ended the weekend in the final playoff position and have a tough final test against Dallas to hang on.

15. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 17

Cincinnati only forced one save out of Andre Blake, but with the help of Roman Celentano's six stops, they booked their playoff spot with a 1-0 win against the Union. Ayoub Jabbari came off the bench in the second half and registered the sole tally of the night, capitalizing on Blake's save (a low-struck ball from Evander) to score off the rebound.

16. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 16

The Dynamo could secure home advantage in the playoffs with a top-of-the-table finish, but are hanging on to fifth place ahead of the final day after losing 3-1 to Portland (their first loss in six). They have a decisive meeting with St. Louis on the final day, who are just ahead of them on goal difference but tied on points.

17. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 19

Sergi Roberto's first MLS goal was the icing on the cake of a 4-1 win against Austin that also featured Hirving Lozano's first goal back from injury and three assists from Marco Reus. Austin's not the toughest opponent in MLS this season, but the result matters as the Galaxy head into the final weekend still competing for a playoff spot.

18. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 20

The Crew may have lost the U.S. Open Cup final, but after beating D.C United 3-0, they're finishing the regular season on a five-game win streak. They confirmed their spot in the postseason and finished the weekend in one of the Eastern Conference's two wild card positions.

19. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 22

The Timbers secured a massive three points in a 3-1 win against the Dynamo highlighted by two assists and a goal from Vincent Janssen (nearly half his total goal contributions this year). With one game remaining, they're in a wild card spot and have one tentative hand on the playoffs.

20. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 23

In his first start since September, Joaquín Pereyra powered the Loons to three points with two goals against LAFC in a 3-1 win. They're still short of a final playoff spot (by two points) but following this result, they can still potentially break in with a win (and other results going in their favor), with San Jose waiting on the final day.

21. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

After falling behind 2-0 early to San Jose, Juan Manuel Sanabria's headed goal (his second of the year) in the 23rd minute provided life, but unfortunately nothing followed. They're currently outside the wild card spots ahead of a crucial final game against the Galaxy, but will also need some results to go their way.

22. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 12

RBNY had an early penalty stopped but came out with the upper hand against Nashville, taking a 2-0 lead in Tennessee that started with a beautiful link up between league wonderkids Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall. But after two own goals and a stoppage-time winner from Nashville, the Red Bulls were eliminated from the playoffs in consecutive seasons for the first time ever.

23. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 21

After conceding a 91st-minute goal to last-placed Montréal, the Pigeons' playoff chances are officially over. A 1-1 draw isn't enough to launch them into the wild card position with one more game to go.

24. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 26

Dreyer -- a back-to-back MLS All-Star -- won't feature in this year's postseason, but that didn't stop him from handing the recently-crowded U.S. Open Cup champions a loss in a 1-0 victory over St. Louis. Dreyer's left-footed chip from distance was a taste of quality we'll be missing seven days from now.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 24

With no postseason hopes, victories must come from small achievements, like letting Reus assist three goals or having a goalkeeper make six saves while still conceding four.

26. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 25

Toronto succumbed to a 3-1 defeat to Atlanta and ended their postseason dream in the process. Back to the drawing board for Robin Fraser's side, who showed signs of potential earlier in the season.

27. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 28

With the playoffs out of the picture and the all-time goals conceded in a single season record newly secured, SKC still did their best to sabotage Dallas by absconding with a 1-1 draw against a side looking to lock up their top-two finish in the Western Conference.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 29

Miguel Almirón won't appear in this year's playoffs, so he put on an end-of-season show in a 3-1 win against Toronto while eliminating the fellow Eastern Conference team from the playoffs. Five Stripes fans will take what they can get this year.

29. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

After losing to Toronto in the midweek, D.C. played Columbus with the playoffs already out of the picture and proceeded to lose 3-0. With 11 years since their last postseason victory, there's nowhere to go but up for this MLS original.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

It's too late to save their season, but not too late to sink somebody else's. A 91st-minute response to NYCFC's 1-0 lead secured their 26th point of the year and put to rest New York's postseason dream.

stories.headline: Chris Fagan to join the Blues as director of coaching in 2027
stories.summary: Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.
stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: Ponga back for NZ as Walsh wins Aussie fullback role
stories.summary: Australian coach Kevin Walters has shown his hand with a big fullback call as New Zealand superstar Kayln Ponga returns for the Rugby League World Cup semis.
stories.body:
Kayln Ponga and Reece Walsh are on track to resume their compelling rivalry after two huge coach calls ahead of the Rugby League World Cup semifinals.

Ponga has been named on New Zealand's extended bench for Saturday night's do-or-die showdown with Tonga in Newcastle, just 22 days after breaking his forearm in a dazzling fullback duel with Walsh in the tournament opener.

And Walsh on Tuesday retained the Australian No.1 jumper ahead of James Tedesco for the Kangaroos' semi-final against Samoa in Sydney on Sunday.

While young gun Keono Kini will again start as custodian at McDonald Jones Stadium, Ponga's inclusion is a firm indication the Newcastle Knights superstar will return for the final should the Kiwis make it.

Coach Stacey Jones also selected hooker Phoenix Crossland among the Kiwis' extended reserves as Australian Test coach Kevin Walters made the most significant move of his tenure by picking Walsh over Tedesco.

The selection dilemma has bubbled along through Australia's three group-stage wins.

Tedesco entered the World Cup in exceptional form after helping the Sydney Roosters to the NRL premiership, while Walsh had spent the last two months on the sidelines with an ankle injury.

But Walsh - the star of last year's Ashes series - has done enough to win the backing of former Broncos coach Walters for the business end of the tournament.

Walsh and Ponga were both electrifying in Australia's 24-22 win over New Zealand last month, before Walsh was man of the match with a hand in five tries in last Saturday's 66-6 rout of the Cook Islands.

In other key Australian selections, Bradman Best has made the left centre spot his own by seeing off the challenge of South Sydney talisman Latrell Mitchell.

Tedesco and Mitchell are both part of a six-man bench that includes Canberra's Ethan Strange and Cameron Murray for the likely Allianz Stadium sell-out.

Tom Dearden and Cameron Munster will line up together in the halves.

"Samoa were very impressive in a physical battle which had a lot of emotion last weekend against Tonga and we know we are in for a tough contest on Sunday night," Walters said.

"It's going to be a great occasion in front of a full house at Allianz Stadium, and we've got to meet the occasion with our best performance of the tournament."

Samoa have made just one enforced change with Ronald Volkman replacing Chanel Harris-Tavita (hamstring) at five-eighth.

In the other semi-final, Tonga are unchanged while Crossland remains an option to feature for the first time since his four-match suspension for his leg-breaking tackle on Nathan Cleary in the NRL preliminary final.

The Newcastle hooker was officially elevated to New Zealand's squad on Monday night after forward Jacob Laban was ruled out with injury.

Jones has named Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad on the wing as a result of Ronaldo Mulitalo's one-game ban for a shoulder charge against Fiji.

stories.headline: Fantasy buzz: No stopping Bears, Seahawks ease Charbonnet back, Minshew impact
stories.summary: The Bears' offense is full of must-start players, Seahawks backfield still in flux as Charbonnet, Price return
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Nov. 3: Bears roster full of must-starts, Seahawks ease Charbonnet back into mix

By Michael F. Florio

The Bears' offense continued rolling on the road against the Super Bowl champs. D'Andre Swift was the star of the show, turning 30 opportunities into 79 yards and three touchdowns. He finished with 23 fantasy points and surely saved many fantasy teams from the jaws of defeat. Luther Burden III stayed hot, turning nine targets into seven catches for 56 yards and a touchdown. He finished with 18.6 fantasy points and has averaged 19.9 fantasy points per game since Caleb Williams returned. He has emerged as the Bears' top pass catcher and is a weekly start. Colston Loveland also saw nine targets, catching seven of them for 65 yards. He finished with 11.5 fantasy points. He has averaged 16.6 fantasy points per game since Williams returned. He is a must-start option each week.

Williams played extremely well even if it did not translate to the biggest fantasy game. He was the first QB to throw for more than 200 yards against the Seahawks' defense. In total he finished with 13.98 fantasy points. That is more about the matchup, though. Williams should be started weekly.
Rome Odunze saw six targets, catching four of them for 87 yards. His 12.7 fantasy points is his second-highest mark in a game this season. It's great to see Odunze produce, but he remains the third target. That makes him a low-floor, high-upside flex option.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to be the Seahawks' offense. He saw 11 targets, catching six for 118 yards and a touchdown. He should be in MVP talks and should be viewed as the best WR in fantasy football. He has one game with fewer than 22 fantasy points this season. He has 52% of his teams receiving yards -- no other player even has 40%.
Both Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet returned from injury in Week 9. Price led the way playing 48% of snaps, with 10 carries and four targets. He finished with 37 yards and 5.7 fantasy points. Charbonnet played 36% of snaps, with six carries and four targets. He went for 29 yards and finished with 5.9 fantasy points. They have a better matchup next week against the Cardinals, but splitting the usage leaves them both as purely flex options.
Sam Darnold's struggles continued, but he ended up having a solid fantasy night as Seattle was trailing and had to throw. He finished with 188 passing yards, two touchdowns, one interception and 17.52 fantasy points. Darnold has nine interceptions in his past six games. Still, he is a streaming option next week against the Cardinals, who have allowed the most passing touchdowns in the NFL.

Nov. 2: How the move to Minshew impacts the Cardinals

By Michael F. Florio

The Arizona Cardinals named Gardner Minshew II as their starting quarterback on Monday for the Week 9 game in Seattle against the Seahawks.

Minshew took over for Jacoby Brissett on Sunday against Dallas and threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns in a comeback win against the Cowboys, but faces a much tougher task next week against Seattle.

The biggest question is what this means for the Cardinals' pass catchers, but here's how I expect the switch at QB to impact all positions on offense.

While a QB change always adds some volatility, Trey McBride remains a must-start tight end. McBride is a must start regardless of who the QB is, but Minshew's tendency to target tight ends at a high rate keeps him as an elite option. In both 2023 and 2024, Minshew threw to tight ends 12% of the time, which is actually a higher rate than Brissett this season (10%).
Due to volume, Michael Wilson will remain in play in most matchups. However, next week against Seattle is a week to get him out of your starting lineup. The Cardinals next three weeks are tough matchups for Wilson. Outside of Wilson, fantasy managers should avoid the rest of the Cardinals receivers for the time being.
The running backs could see a bump in targets as well, as Minshew has always targeted running backs at a high rate. His career average is 17%, while Brissett is at 13% this season.
As for Minshew himself, fantasy managers should stay away with the next three weeks being the Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs. For Week 9, some more favorable streaming options are Kyler Murray (or potentially Carson Wentz), Malik Willis, Sam Darnold and C.J. Stroud.

It is worth noting that since 2021, there have been 12 relief performances of 15 or more fantasy points by quarterbacks who went on to make another start at some point in that given season; that group averaged 6.7 fewer fantasy points as starters (shout out to Tristan H. Cockcroft for the stat!).

Nov. 2: Notebook for Week 8

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills

Derrick Henry's playing time has declined over the past two weeks, falling below 50% of snaps against the Bills. On Sunday, he rushed for 53 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, marking his third straight game with fewer than 60 rushing yards. Justice Hill played on more snaps and ran more routes compared to Henry's nine, benefiting from Baltimore playing from behind. With Lamar Jackson headed for IR due to a thumb injury, the Ravens could struggle to sustain drives and generate red zone opportunities, making Henry's fantasy outlook even more concerning going forward.
Dalton Kincaid played through a chest injury against the Ravens and delivered his second-best fantasy performance (18.6 fantasy points) of the season, catching four out of six targets for 86 yards and a touchdown. Kincaid continues to share playing time with Dawson Knox, but his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. He ran 23 routes (compared to Knox's 17) and his targets per route remain high despite a slight decline in snaps. Kincaid has now stockpiled 14 targets over his past two games and remains a solid TE1 heading into Week 9 against the Vikings.

Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals

Wan'Dale Robinson continues to be Tennessee's most reliable receiver. He led the Titans in both snaps and routes against the Bengals, catching six out of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown. He has now drawn at least six targets in four straight games and remains a flex option. Chimere Dike caught five passes for 71 yards and a touchdown while filling in for Carnell Tate, but his role could shrink after the Week 9 bye. TE Gunnar Helm had his best game of the season with five receptions for 76 yards on nine targets, despite playing on a season-low percentage of snaps. Daniel Bellinger's increased involvement makes Helm difficult to trust outside deeper leagues.
Chase Brown led Cincinnati's backfield in snaps, routes and touches against the Titans. Brown finished with 55 rushing yards on 12 carries and caught eight out of nine targets for 46 yards, scoring 16.1 fantasy points. He also ran more than twice as many routes as Samaje Perine, highlighting his significant role in the passing game. Perine finished with just five touches for 19 yards but remains involved in the red zone. Brown's workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 conversation heading into Week 9 against a Falcons defense that ranks among the top five in fantasy points per game allowed to running backs. Perine remains as merely an insurance back.
Mike Gesicki set a season-high in snaps against the Titans following injuries to Erick All Jr. and Tanner Hudson. He ran three times as many routes as Drew Sample, and caught four out of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown (17.6 fantasy points). Gesicki has now scored a touchdown in five straight games, but what's even more encouraging is his increased involvement on early downs and in two-TE sets. With All and Hudson out for the rest of the season, Gesicki's expanded role should continue. He's worth adding for fantasy managers needing help at tight end.
Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions

The Vikings used a three-man backfield against the Lions, with no running back playing more than 40% of snaps. Aaron Jones Sr. led the way, followed by DeeJay Dallas and Jordan Mason. Mason led the backfield with eight carries for 20 yards, while Jones had five carries for 22 yards and caught both of his targets for 18 yards. Dallas handled most of the third-down work but finished with just one touch. Jones and Mason remain difficult to trust as anything more than flex options until their roles become clearer. However, the Vikings face a Bills defense in Week 9 that has allowed the fourth-most RB fantasy points per game.
Jordan Addison has seen increased playing time in the slot over the last two games, giving him more opportunities in the Vikings passing game. Against the Lions, Addison led Minnesota receivers in snaps and caught three out of eight targets for 11.6 fantasy points. Justin Jefferson led the team with nine targets, while Jauan Jennings had just two. Addison's eight targets were a season high, which is encouraging for managers. The Vikings face the Bills and Packers over their next two games, both of whom rank among the top 10 in terms of the most WR fantasy points per game.

Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys

Tyler Allgeier took over Arizona's backfield against the Cowboys after Jeremiyah Love aggravated his ankle injury and Bam Knight suffered a concussion. Love opened the game as the primary back, with Knight taking over early-down work following his departure. Once Knight exited, Allgeier played every running back snap in the second half and overtime. He finished with 147 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, adding five receptions for 44 yards and another score for a season-high 36.1 fantasy points. Allgeier should be a priority waiver pickup with RB2 upside if Love and Knight miss Week 9 against the Seahawks. His performance could also earn him a larger role even when both return.
Arizona's receiving corps continues to battle injuries. Kendrick Bourne suffered an ankle injury, Reggie Virgil exited late, and Michael Wilson played through broken ribs. Trey McBride and Wilson dominated snaps and routes, with Wilson drawing a team-high 15 targets and finishing with 111 yards and a touchdown. McBride added seven receptions for 72 yards and a score. He's now caught at least seven passes in 10 straight games -- the third-longest streak in NFL history. Both remain must-start fantasy options as targets continue to be concentrated between them. Gardner Minshew II also replaced Jacoby Brissett and could start in Week 9.
The Cowboys rank seventh in passing attempts per game, creating plenty of opportunities for their receivers. George Pickens has dealt with shoulder and hamstring injuries over the last two weeks, leading to more frequent substitutions and increased playing time for Ryan Flournoy. When Pickens has rotated out, Flournoy has handled most of the available snaps in single-receiver sets and taken on additional work in two-WR formations. Flournoy has now drawn at least four targets and scored at least 12 fantasy points in four straight games. Monitor Pickens' practice participation this week. If he remains limited, Flournoy could be an intriguing sleeper against a vulnerable Colts defense in Week 9.

Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers

Dylan Sampson led the Browns backfield in snaps, routes run and fantasy points (12.9), largely because Cleveland was playing from behind. Quinshon Judkins still led the backfield with 13 touches, compared to only seven for Sampson. This is something fantasy managers will have to live with when rostering Judkins, whose workload is more favorable when the Browns are playing with a lead or keeping games competitive. Cleveland should have an easier time moving the ball against the Saints in Week 9, keeping Judkins in the volume-based RB2 conversation.
KC Concepcion was held to four targets and 6.7 fantasy points against the Steelers after finishing with 10 targets and a season-high 23.2 fantasy points against the Titans in Week 7. Despite leading Cleveland in routes run, Concepcion was out-targeted by both Harold Fannin Jr. (12) and Denzel Boston (11). The playing time is encouraging, but the inconsistent target volume makes Concepcion and Boston difficult to trust in fantasy lineups. Fannin has been the more reliable option, drawing at least nine targets and scoring at least 13 fantasy points in consecutive games. He remains a low-end TE1.

Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets

The Raiders made a surprising change in their backfield against the Jets, giving Mike Washington Jr. the start over Ashton Jeanty. Washington dominated early-down and goal-line work, finishing with 83 rushing yards on a career-high 25 carries after never having reached double-digit attempts in any previous game this season. Jeanty played on a season-low number of snaps, managing just 9 yards on two carries but catching three passes for 64 yards. Coach Klint Kubiak said the change wasn't disciplinary and expects both backs to remain involved. Washington should be a priority waiver pickup, while Jeanty's reduced workload makes him a riskier fantasy option.
Braelon Allen led the Jets' backfield in snaps, routes and touches (23), finishing with a season-high 23.3 fantasy points. Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game, despite practicing on a limited basis throughout the week. Allen remains a must-hold for fantasy managers regardless of whether Hall is traded or stays in New York. He's played well enough to maintain a significant role, either as the lead back or in a committee with Hall. The Jets also have one of the more favorable remaining schedules for running backs, particularly after their Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs, making Allen worth holding for the stretch run.
Adonai Mitchell had a breakout performance against the Raiders, catching seven of his nine targets for 27.2 fantasy points. Garrett Wilson led the Jets with 12 targets, finishing with 14.3. Omar Cooper Jr. wasn't targeted, despite playing more snaps than Mitchell. Cooper continues to get more opportunities in two-WR sets, although Mitchell ran more routes against the Raiders. Mitchell will be a target on waivers, but the competition for playing time makes both receivers difficult to trust consistently. Wilson remains the safest fantasy option in this receiving corps.

Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars

The Colts continued to lean on Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs against the Jaguars despite trade rumors surrounding both players. Taylor played on 79% of snaps before garbage time but finished with just 12 touches and 6.7 fantasy points. Downs led Indianapolis in routes and caught four out of five targets for 12.3 fantasy points, thanks to a receiving touchdown. His playing time increased as the Colts used more three-WR sets while playing from behind. Their fantasy outlooks could change considerably, depending on what happens before the trade deadline.
Tyler Warren returned after missing the past two games due to a groin injury and led the Colts' TE room in snaps, routes, targets (10) and fantasy points (5.8). He saw a slight dip in playing time against the Jaguars compared to the first five weeks of the season, as Will Mallory took some additional snaps in 11 personnel. Although Warren had his second-worst fantasy performance of the season, he could take on a larger role in the Colts offense if either Taylor or Downs is traded.

Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown against the Falcons, finishing with 21 fantasy points. Irving and Kenny Gainwell split snaps evenly after Irving played on 64% of snaps over the first seven weeks. Irving remained the primary early-down back with 27 carries, while Gainwell handled all the passing-down snaps and rushed for 140 yards on 25 attempts. Poor weather conditions led Tampa Bay to run the ball on 90% of its plays, so I wouldn't expect this kind of split every week. Irving remains a must-start, having scored at least 21 fantasy points in three of his last four games.
Kyle Pitts Sr. has seen a slight dip in playing time over the last two weeks as he continues to split snaps with Charlie Woerner and Nick Muse, but his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. He's drawn at least five targets in four straight games and scored at least 13 fantasy points in three of them.

Los Angeles Chargers at Los Angeles Rams

Kyren Williams led the Rams backfield in snaps, routes and touches (17), but Blake Corum led the way with 13.3 fantasy points. Corum finished with 11 touches and both backs scored rushing touchdowns. Corum averaged 6.6 yards per carry, compared to 3.3 for Williams. He has now scored at least 13 fantasy points in four straight games and handled at least 10 touches in three of them. The Rams continue to lean heavily on their running game, keeping both Williams and Corum fantasy relevant.
The Chargers continued their three-man backfield rotation against the Rams, with Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell splitting early-down work while Kimani Vidal handled passing situations. Vidal led the backfield in snaps and routes run, while Mitchell and Hampton saw similar playing time. Hampton finished with 27 total yards on 11 touches, while Vidal had 30 yards on 10 touches and Mitchell added 23 yards on seven touches. The Chargers offense has been a disaster, ranking last in points, touchdowns and turnovers this season. Limited opportunities and a three-man rotation make this a backfield fantasy managers should continue to avoid.

Kansas City Chiefs at Denver Broncos

Jonah Coleman took control of the Broncos backfield against the Chiefs with RJ Harvey sidelined by a knee injury. Coleman led the Broncos backfield in snaps and routes and finished with 41 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, adding four receptions for 63 yards (20.4 fantasy points). J.K. Dobbins managed just 13 yards on seven carries. Coleman also handled goal-line work and most of the second-half snaps, making him a must-add and a solid RB2 heading into Week 9 against a Panthers defense that's allowed the second-most RB fantasy points per game.
It was frustrating for Kenneth Walker III's fantasy managers to see Emmett Johnson finish with six touches and 25.3 fantasy points, compared to Walker's 25 touches and 12.3 fantasy points. However, context is important. Johnson played on a season-low number of snaps against the Broncos, while Walker continues to dominate touches in Kansas City's backfield. Walker has handled at least 20 touches in seven out of eight games this season. Johnson remains one of the top insurance backs worth rostering, but Walker's consistent workload should keep fantasy managers confident in his outlook.

New England Patriots at Miami Dolphins

DeMario Douglas led Patriots pass catchers with 16.6 fantasy points while A.J. Brown was ruled out and Romeo Doubs remained on IR. Douglas tied for the second-most routes run despite ranking fourth in snaps among New England's pass catchers. However, he's played primarily in 11 personnel this season, which could make his weekly production inconsistent, despite the strong performance.
Ollie Gordon II remains the Dolphins' clear lead back, playing on more than 80% of offensive snaps for the second straight week. He rushed for 69 yards on 19 carries against the Patriots but failed to catch his only target, finishing with 6.9 fantasy points. Gordon handled a season-high share of early-down snaps despite Jaylen Wright being fully healthy, while Kaytron Allen didn't see any offensive snaps. Gordon has averaged nearly 18 touches over his last four games, keeping him in the RB2 conversation. However, he has caught just one pass during that stretch, making him heavily dependent on rushing production and touchdowns.

Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders

The Commanders adjusted their receiving rotation with Terry McLaurin on IR. Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams took over as Washington's primary outside receivers against the Eagles. Both played season-high shares of snaps and ran more routes than Stefon Diggs, who continued to work primarily from the slot. Burks caught three passes for 81 yards, while Williams led the team with seven targets, finishing with five receptions for 54 yards. Diggs caught three passes for 38 yards and a touchdown. Burks and Williams are worth adding in deeper leagues, while Diggs remains a TD-dependent flex option heading into a difficult Week 9 matchup against the Rams.

Oct. 30: Packers' ground game cause for concern

By Adam Rank

Jordan Love throws multiple touchdown passes. Matthew Golden looks good. I mean, Christian Watson left and arrived back at Lambeau Field from an ambulance in a move that would make Triple H say, "no way this is real." And yet, I get a note from my editor (a Packers fan, mind you) complaining about the (lack of a) Green Bay Packers running game.

I mean, the Milwaukee Brewers just won the World Series, but we need to focus on the Packers' rushing attack? Well, I guess that is the best place to start.

The Packers won the game despite rushing for just 66 yards. They have been held to fewer than 90 rushing yards in all eight games, the club's longest streak in the Super Bowl era. The Packers' 485 rushing yards are the fewest by any team through eight games since the 2019 Bengals. I mean, what in the name of Eddie Lee Ivery is going on here?

The short answer is the offensive line is bad. The playcalling is bad. I mean, you think the guy who favored Dion Lewis over Derrick Henry when he was offensive coordinator in Tennessee was ever going to have a solid running game in Green Bay? It's just the facts.

And it's not going to get much easier in the coming weeks, either. The New England Patriots, Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Rams aren't great matchups. It's not until the New Orleans Saints in Week 13 that the schedule softens for Josh Jacobs. If you kept him on your roster all this time, you're likely going to be compelled to start him, but the matchups aren't ideal.

Some other notes from Thursday night:

Love has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all eight games this season, but this was his first game of the season with three touchdown passes. He's a set-and-forget quarterback moving forward. It is wild to think he wasn't drafted as a QB1 this year.
Watson is nearing ace territory this season. He recorded his 12th reception of 20-plus yards, second in the league behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Golden is also a must-start, but he registered two drops Thursday. Love has seen 20 drops by his receivers this season. I feel like that total would double if you counted the number of interceptions that are dropped. Or maybe it just seems that way to me, a Bears supporter.
Is the "Bryce Young as a QB1" era over already? Well, for starters, the Carolina Panthers need to do a better job of protecting him. He was hit. A lot. I'm not rushing him back into my lineup next week against the Denver Broncos. You might want to take a look at the waiver wire right now for a streamable option if Young is your only quarterback. Kyler Murray against the Buffalo Bills next week could do the trick.
Chuba Hubbard was good, however. He scored a touchdown, rushed for 81 yards and caught seven balls for 38 more yards. Again, playing the Bills next week makes him a prime RB1.

stories.headline: How the Knicks' season, title defense got chaotic -- fast
stories.summary: New York has stayed in the headlines -- for all the wrong reasons. Can the 2026 champs bounce back?
stories.body:
THE VISUAL WAS telling, if not stark.

The Philadelphia 76ers moved the ball all over their NBA Cup-adorned court while the New York Knicks scrambled to catch up, reminiscent of how the reigning champions ran things in the second round of last season's playoffs when they won 15 of their final 16 games, including 13 straight.

This time, the Knicks weren't taking over Xfinity Mobile Arena. They didn't get 3-pointers from Josh Hart or Miles McBride or Jalen Brunson after good ball movement. Instead, 76ers star Tyrese Maxey was driving down the lane for an easy dunk.

Sixers fans chanted "MVP" for Maxey instead of being drowned out by their rivals who made the trek down I-95. LeBron James, after a tip-in that sealed the game, basked in the love as the newest addition to this rivalry. And after Philadelphia handed New York its fourth loss of the season, a 98-93 defeat, Hart carried a bloody bruise atop his freshly braided head.

Heavy is the head that wears the crown.

If "easy" was the word used to describe the Knicks' spring, they haven't had a moment of ease since. Off the court, the team has been plagued by headlines about contract extension talks being paused for its stars until season's end and championship ring controversy. On the court, they've posted a 3-4 record, ranked 22nd in offense, and shot 35.7% from 3-point range, slightly above league average.

Early returns have the Knicks often looking like two different teams within the same night, sometimes the same quarter. Before, when the Knicks would go on one of those devastating runs of ball-popping offense and suffocating defense, teams would cower.

You could feel it. Momentum building, an almost inevitable feeling that everything would eventually go the Knicks' way -- a massive factor in their record 14.9 point differential in the playoffs.

Now, teams merely wait out the Knicks, knowing an opening is coming.

"One thing I see, when we get those runs, we start to look like the team we've been in the past. [Then] we get a little comfortable," Brunson said following the loss to the Orlando Magic. "We've got to continue to put our foot on the gas and execute like we did last year."

Coach Mike Brown didn't deny his team has gotten off to a lethargic start. His task of getting this team to repeat as champions is tough enough: The parity era of eight champions in the past eight years is the longest such stretch in NBA history. Only last season's Thunder even made it out of the second round in pursuit of defending their title.

It could be the competition catching up to the Knicks, or the uncertainty of player contracts having a very human effect. But to his credit, Brown is focusing on the long game and not the panic that can set in with a misfortunate start to the season.

"This is a new season. It's a new team, and we're going to have challenges in front of us," Brown said. "It's like climbing a mountain. You know, sometimes you go 100 yards, but you might get knocked back 5 yards.

"You regroup as a team, and you figure out how to keep going forward the right way by making sure we embrace the process."

IT'S NOT UNCOMMON to see Hart stewing after a bad game or a bad stretch. More than his buddy-cop relationship with Brunson, he is the emotional center of the Knicks and has been since he arrived in 2023 at the trade deadline.

When the Knicks lost three straight games late last season, culminating in a 17-point road loss to the Rockets in Houston, Hart called it out, claiming the next night in Memphis was a must-win game.

"We're not going in the right direction," he said that evening.

The Knicks responded by winning the next five games before resting their regulars in the season finale, paving the way for their dominant playoff run.

Hart doesn't mind saying the uncomfortable thing. But with his contract status up in the air, will he hesitate should an issue arise?

"I guarantee you, I'm going to be sitting here rock bottom," Hart told ESPN. "I don't think I'm ever going to be on my high horse, either.

"We're in New York. Everything rides on the next game. We go on a 10-game winning streak and the next game we lose, they're ready to burn the place down. We know what it is. It's the tough part of being in New York."

Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla, whose team handed the Knicks their second loss of this season, understands how hard it is to move past a loss.

"I don't think the psychological wars ever end after a game, I think it goes on for you as long as you're in it," Mazzulla said. "Every team brings in scars from the past."

Brown has pointed to on-ball defense, indecision on offense and his players standing around when plays break down as culprits for the slow start. According to NBA.com, the Knicks trail only the Houston Rockets and Charlotte Hornets in frequency of shots late in the shot clock (four seconds or less), and shooting 28.8% in those situations ranks them behind only the Portland Trail Blazers in efficiency -- they were best in the league last season.

Usually, that's Brunson time, as he did so often in the playoffs. But the magic hasn't been there to start the season.

The Knicks haven't come back from big deficits the way they did last season, when they rallied from double digits in six playoff games, the largest being a 29-point comeback over the San Antonio Spurs to win Game 4 of the Finals.

Have they lulled themselves into a false sense of security with all those improbable comebacks? Will they dig themselves a hole too deep to emerge, and what's the cost of playing that way consistently?

"I've said in the past it's important to learn from wins, obviously, you learn from losses as well," Brunson said Friday in Philadelphia. "There's been plenty of times we learned from being down what we can do. And in that same game, made adjustments to where we weren't down anymore. We have to put a full 48 minutes together."

The 76ers, a team still building sweat equity after trading for Jaylen Brown and James in the offseason, exposed what appears to be the Knicks' kryptonite: speed.

"Sometimes it takes us a little longer to get into the game. Whether that's the flow, whether that's fatigue," Hart said. "Not relying on these comebacks because it's taxing."

"We all feel the fatigue. We've got to fight through it. It's six games in, we've got to find a way to get our bodies ready to play. Mentally we're there; we've got find it physically."

When Brunson was asked about it, he dismissed it flippantly: "Josh said he feels the fatigue? Josh is old as s---."

It is not just Brunson and Hart who bear those scars. It took swingman Mikal Bridges four games before he connected on a 3-pointer, and seven games before he even attempted a free throw. Finals MVP Brunson is shooting at career-low marks from the field and from 3.

And Brown is toggling between Andre Drummond and James Wiseman as backup centers in an effort to replace Mitchell Robinson, who signed a free agent deal with the Celtics when the cost-conscious Knicks failed to retain him. New York has felt the impact of losing Mitchell, particularly in efficiency: Robinson shot 72% from the field in 2025-26, while Drummond hit 47% last season and is shooting just 46% so far in this one. Wiseman is 0-5 from the field.

McBride said it's not just up to Brunson and Hart to speak up; this team is self-aware and mature enough to have those hard conversations.

"It's open," McBride told ESPN. "Anybody can step up, whether it's the [bench] guys or starters. That's the thing about this team, our chemistry is so good and we have a lot of trust because we see each other putting forth a lot of work."

Brown, for his part, is not afraid to speak up, either.

When the Knicks' season reached a breaking point last spring, down 2-1 to the Atlanta Hawks in the first round, Brown challenged Towns to get the ball more and be aggressive with it. It turned around their entire fortunes and led to the record playoff winning streak and finish through the NBA Finals.

"I'm going to keep it real," Brown said in early October. "If there's something in front of us, I'm not a fan of having an elephant in the room. I'll address it. I don't care if it's Jalen or KAT or OG [Anunoby]."

The Knicks won't catch anyone off guard this time. And their 3-4 record has them ranked No. 8 in the East.

Perhaps for his own sanity, Brown said he evaluates the season in five-game increments. Brunson believes the first month or so of games will be revealing.

"I think everyone in the East knows each other," Towns told ESPN. "This is our third year now with each other, so you know, it's rare. That's one of our advantages."

He compared it to James going to the Miami Heat in summer 2010 and how it changed the tone of the East for the entire decade.

"At the end of the day, people knew, when LeBron and the big three were there, you had to go out there and beat them," Towns said. "Everyone brings their best against the New York Knicks. You've got to protect the jersey, the city at all costs."

BROWN KEPT A steely face, giving nothing away when asked whether he had received his championship ring -- the latest in a string of less-than-flattering headlines since the team's title in June.

It had been over a week since news broke that New York assistant coaches did not receive their championship rings on opening night. Additionally, some employees who had yet to receive their rings had been sent a phishing email from Madison Square Garden security that stated their "Employee Championship Ring is here."

"I'm not going to talk about that ring stuff, as you can imagine," Brown said, despite speculation that the ring box he was handed was either empty or contained someone else's ring. "I'm not going to get into any of that."

It's true to Brown's character. In his first year as Knicks coach, his gift was his ability to avoid making waves -- and lead the team to its first championship in 53 years, of course.

Brown knows the path to another ring will be even harder. He saw it firsthand as an assistant coach with the Golden State Warriors, who added Kevin Durant to a team that had won 73 regular-season games the season before. The Warriors cruised through the playoffs in 2017, winning their first 15 games, but the next season they were nearly knocked out of the conference finals by the Rockets.

And that was before the NBA's rules made it harder for teams to establish and maintain dominance.

But even more telling is that fact that the teams that have repeated since the millennium have been headlined by James, Shaquille O'Neal, Kobe Bryant and Stephen Curry -- players on the short list of all-timers.

Fittingly, Mazzulla understands the road Brown is journeying. After a 64-win season that culminated in a 16-3 run through the playoffs and the 2024 NBA title, Mazzulla's Celtics followed it up with 61 wins in 2025, entering the playoffs as a defending champion many believed had a great chance at repeating.

But they ran into the Knicks in the Eastern Conference semifinals, and the atrophy of the previous few seasons began to show. Jayson Tatum was the biggest casualty, tearing his right Achilles in Game 4 in New York as he desperately tried to get the Celtics back into a series they'd fallen behind in.

"That's the competitive realm you're in. Once you're there, you have to trick yourself as if you've never been there," Mazzulla said. "But at the same time, two years away from that, every loss is more painful than it was three years ago. You have to treat yourself as if you're more desperate than everybody else."

But the additional games add up, along with the breakneck pace of today's NBA. That has potentially played a part in the fate of the 2025 champion Thunder, who have four rotation players dealing with major injuries that could derail their season. Like Mazzulla's Celtics, who went to the Finals in 2022 before their breakthrough win in 2024, the Thunder have stacked multiple deep playoff runs -- a problem this Knicks team is also facing.

Brunson has played 61 playoff games since coming to New York -- 37 in the past two seasons. Same for Hart. Anunoby joined the Knicks three years ago and has played 44 postseason games with the franchise and 71 overall dating back to his days in Toronto. Towns reached the conference finals in Minnesota the season before being traded to the Knicks, so that adds up to 53 games in the past three seasons.

The bill on that could come due sooner than anyone expected.

The Knicks are in contract limbo with three key players, after tabling all contract extension talks on Oct. 9. Owner James Dolan said this summer that New York wouldn't dip into the punitive second apron to keep the team together.

Hart has a team option and on media day said there hadn't been any discussions on a new deal. Towns is eligible for a four-year, $276 million deal. Before talks were halted, the Knicks' offer was at $200 million, which represents a pay cut from his current salary (four years, $220.4 million).

Towns hoped for a contract extension at the start of last season and didn't get it. The disappointment was quiet, but he played through an up-and-down regular season as he and Brown struggled to get on the same page; then it clicked in the postseason.

He's prepared for a similar process.

"I mean, we did it all last year," Towns told ESPN. "You're in New York, you've got to play through distractions; that's what comes with playing here. There's a lot of pressure, a lot of noise."

"But as long as this locker room, which has shown it can do, stays together and continues to just believe and fall into each other when things get tough, we can do something special."

Towns pointed to the Knicks' struggles after they won the NBA Cup last season, an ugly 2-9 stretch from Dec. 31 to Jan. 19, as proof they're built to handle adversity.

"We didn't look our best version, and we heard about it," Towns said. "This team continued to fall into each other instead of splitting away and ... separating. We got closer and closer."

In Philadelphia, Towns said: "We have to find a way to be that magical team we were last year. You don't want to wait to find that magic. Lightning don't strike twice."

stories.headline: The 10 most iconic moments of the 2026 season, as told by WNBA Art
stories.summary: WNBA Art, the viral Instagram account from artist Meg Stacy, documented the best moments of the WNBA season.
stories.body:
Rhyne Howard jumped, reached her arm up and swatted away 6-foot-11 Han Xu's shot. The 6-2 Howard's block against a player 9 inches taller than her was a highlight of the Atlanta Dream's 85-83 win, which completed their semifinal sweep of the New York Liberty. But the reaction from Howard's teammate Allisha Gray,on the bench -- eyes open wide and lips pursed, impressed -- drew more attention.

"That's going to be a WNBA Art drawing after this," ESPN analyst Rebecca Lobo said on the broadcast during a replay of Gray's reaction.

Meg Stacy, the Chicago-area artist behind the viral WNBA Art account on Instagram, obliged. She drew Howard's block with Gray's face in the foreground and posted it with the caption "what rebecca lobo said..."

Receiving a shout-out on national TV during a playoff game is a normal part of Stacy's life now. She has been featured on Sue Bird's podcast, invited to WNBA All-Star Weekend and has met several current and former WNBA players.

"The whole thing is wild," Stacy said. "I'm like in their world now."

But it's a far cry from when she made her first WNBA Art post on May 9: a smiling cartoon basketball and the words "Watch this space."

Stacy documented the most impressive, heartwarming and meme-able moments of the 2026 WNBA season. With the season now over and the Golden State Valkyries crowned champions, we're putting on our big WNBA Art googly eyes to look back at 10 of the most iconic moments of the season.

Investigate Olivia Miles (June 18)
Olivia Miles' dominance from the start of her rookie year was one of 2026's top storylines. On May 14, less than a week into the season, Stacy drew a picture of Miles -- the No. 2 pick in April's draft by the Minnesota Lynx -- next to the words "2026 ROTY?" A month later, Miles continued confounding fans with her talent, leading to Stacy's version of the "Charlie Conspiracy" meme from "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia." Charlie tries to uncover the truth about Miles' rookie status. How could a rookie be that good? There was no adequate response to that question throughout the season -- except to award Miles the 2026 Rookie of the Year.

Crashout Jar (July 12)
Regarding her favorite posts, Stacy said, "I like any of the pieces that are really niche and very 'if you know you know' and real fans would find them hilarious." Her July 12 drawing of the Toronto Tempo's Marina Mabrey putting money into her "crashout jar" with a shoe flying in the background would certainly qualify. Mabrey introduced the jar in a January YouTube video as an accountability tool to quell her fiery outbursts on the court: $1 for curse words, $40 for a scuffle and varying prices for other offenses. And the shoe? It hit Mabrey after Betnijah Laney-Hamilton threw it toward teammate Jonquel Jones in a July 12 game between the Liberty and the Tempo. Mabrey has yet to announce the final total of 2026's crashout jar.

Dunked (July 26)
Dominique Malonga's dunking ability started making headlines even before the Seattle Storm drafted her into the WNBA. So fans were eager to see her do it in her first All-Star Game. Malonga didn't disappoint, dunking off an assist from Team Coop teammate Angel Reese in the second quarter. The two are shown jumping and celebrating moments after the slam. Stacy emphasized the importance of love in her art: "For me, the league that I love and the fandom that I have around me, we really do lean into the love between the players and the love of the game."

A'ja vs. CC (Aug. 7)
Although most WNBA Art posts capture iconic moments outside of gameplay, there are reminders that fierce on-court competition defines the W. How better to demonstrate this than a drawing of two of the top players in the league going at it? In an Aug. 6 game between the Las Vegas Aces and Indiana Fever, Caitlin Clark threw the ball up, but 2026 MVP A'ja Wilson swatted it up and away. The two are shown here jumping, reaching to capture it, with Wilson winning the battle as the Aces went on to defeat Indiana 86-84 in overtime.

Dat Way (Aug. 19)
Reese's historic season was at the forefront of W conversations as the Defensive Player of the Year helped guide Atlanta to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. But she was a mainstay on WNBA Art for other reasons. "I am an Angel Reese fan," Stacy said. "But people would assume on my page, 'You must be obsessed with Angel Reese.' No, she just gives moments all the time that are meme-able that you have to cover." WNBA Art's most-liked post of the season depicts Reese in an Aug. 18 game versus the Aces showing exactly which way the possession arrow should go.

Calm Down (Aug. 20)
Generating iconic moments on and off the court seems second nature for Paige Bueckers. At the end of the first half of the Dallas Wings' 91-85 win over Indiana on Aug. 20, Bueckers committed an intentional foul on Clark, which the Fever star did not appreciate. Clark threw the ball and shouted in Bueckers' direction, to which two-time All-Star Bueckers replied, "Calm down," with an outstretched arm. "me @ everyone for everything all the time" Stacy captioned the post.

The Sun Sets (Sept. 23)
Not all WNBA Art drawings are memorable in a fun way. Before the Connecticut Sun played their final game on Sept. 24 to a sold-out crowd at Mohegan Sun Arena, Stacy said she cried as she posted this "sunset" picture. "My heart goes out to Connecticut and their fans," she said. "Drawing that piece made me so emotional and that got a lot of messages from people that shared all these moments with family growing up ... If you look at the comments on that post, [there is] someone who shared special memories with their mom who had passed away. ... It's so beautiful that people can be brought together like that." The Sun are relocating to become the Houston Comets this offseason.

Clutch Gene (Oct. 1)
Has Arike Ogunbowale always been clutch? (Spoiler alert: yes.) On the left, Ogunbowale sinks a game-tying 3-pointer over Gabby Williams to force overtime in Game 2 of Dallas' first-round playoff series against Golden State. On the right, a collegiate Ogunbowale (who had been defended by Williams until a screen caused a defensive switch just moments before) sinks a game-winning jumper in overtime of Notre Dame's 2018 NCAA Final Four win against UConn. There's a heartwarming sense of nostalgia here for any fans who have watched players like Ogunbowale grow from college to the pros. And there's a sense that Williams, known as a defensive specialist, wouldn't find any part of this picture heartwarming.

Right Hand Blue (Oct. 8)
There was another game within Game 2 of the LibertyDream semifinal series. As the two teams got tangled up, it looked like they were playing Twister and Breanna Stewart was tasked with "Right hand blue!" Stacy explained that as her account grew, the messages she received from fans consistently used one word: levity. "They kept saying, 'Thank you for bringing levity. You're the levity that we needed. ... Levity, levity, levity,'" Stacy said. "So I think as the season progressed [bringing levity] became the goal."

Champions (Oct. 31)
On Halloween -- in front of a Chase Center crowd dubbed Boohalla for the holiday -- the Valkyries became WNBA champions in just their second season. They also became the first team to win the championship in a season without an All-WNBA selection. Finals MVP Williams' 30 points tied for the most points in a winner-take-all Finals game and helped lead Golden State to victory. Two Valkyrie swords triumphantly make the A in "champions" to close out a memorable 2026 season.

What's next?
Now that the offseason is upon us, what's next for Stacy and WNBA Art? "No offseason," she said. She has plans to expand her coverage to Unrivaled and other women's sports leagues and to collaborate with WNBA and women's college teams.

"Maybe one day throw a man in there, I know that's not my demographic," Stacy said. "I might test the water at some point and throw an NBA Art out there and see how people react to it. But obviously the big draw is women's sports when it comes to my page, so I do plan on continuing coverage, and I really don't see any stopping coming any time soon."

stories.headline: Boy, 14, arrested for Bradley Lowery taunt at Sunderland fans
stories.summary: A 14-year-old boy has been arrested after social media footage appeared to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland supporters about Bradley Lowery.
stories.body:
A 14-year-old boy has been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and subsequently bailed after social media footage appeared to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland supporters about Bradley Lowery.

Black Cats fan Bradley captured the hearts of the football world when he was diagnosed with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer. He died at the age of six in 2017.

Social media footage showed a fan holding up a photo of Bradley during Saturday's Premier League match between Coventry and Sunderland.

West Midlands Police said in a statement on Tuesday: "A teenage boy arrested on suspicion of a public order offence in Coventry has been bailed with conditions."

On Sunday Bradley's mum Gemma Lowery issued an emotional statement through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, urging people not to "direct any hate, threats or harm" towards the teenage boy or his family.

She said her "beautiful boy" Bradley "deserves to be remembered with love, not hate", adding: "To see such a beautiful memory [the photo] used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

"We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I'm all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?

"I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad's family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don't want hatred directed towards him, so please please don't, just for him to learn from this.

"Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day."

The police said on Sunday the boy had handed himself in.

In that statement, the police added: "We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim's family and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs."

Coventry said they were aware of the social media footage and added: "The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action."

stories.headline: Barcelona lift ban on supporters' group for Aston Villa clash
stories.summary: Barcelona has lifted a ban on different supporters' groups ahead of Tuesday's Champions League home game against Aston Villa following a positive meeting.
stories.body:
Barcelona has lifted a ban on different supporters' groups ahead of Tuesday's Champions League home game against Aston Villa following a positive meeting.

Barça had temporarily banned the operation of 'Gol 1957,' known as the "animation" stand, for Saturday's league match against Alavés after a member of that group struck Real Madrid player Eduardo Camavinga with a flag during the Clásico at the Camp Nou on Oct. 25.

Barcelona executives met on Monday with representatives of those responsible for managing that section before announcing it would reopen that stand.

"The spokespersons have committed the groups to behave in a civic and respectful fashion in the stands," the club said.

"The club values the positive nature of the commitment undertaken by the supporters' group, which plays an important role in backing the team during the game. The club will monitor closely this commitment. Behaviour that led to the ban have brought repeated financial penalties and expose the Club to the possibility of having to close the stadium.

"FC Barcelona is confident that with everyone's commitment, this situation will not be repeated to the good of the members, fans and the club itself."

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli is F1 champion. But why didn't he get his trophy in Mexico City?
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli is F1 world champion, but he won't get his trophy until December. Why does the sport still deny its champions their crowning moment?
stories.body:
There was one rather significant thing missing from Kimi Antonelli's world championship celebrations in Mexico City: the world championship trophy itself.

Despite becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history, the Italian will have to wait until Dec. 12 to get his hands on the prize he has spent his life chasing. That is because, unlike almost every other major sporting competition, F1 does not hand its championship trophy to the winner at the moment of victory. Instead, Antonelli will receive it while wearing a tuxedo, in a sterile hall, at the FIA's annual prize-giving gala dinner in Shanghai in December, six weeks after clinching the title.

It is one of F1's more peculiar traditions, denying the sport the sort of iconic sporting image synonymous with its biggest prizes. Think of the World Cup, the Super Bowl's Vince Lombardi Trophy or NHL's Stanley Cup, just to name three. The moment of triumph and the presentation of the trophy are inseparable. It doesn't have to be a conventional trophy, either. The Masters has turned the previous winner presenting the new winner a green blazer one of the most iconic images in all of sports.

F1's championship trophy, by contrast, seems almost an afterthought. Many fans would struggle to recognise it, which seems crazy for the series which is the pinnacle of motor racing.

It is a shame, too, because it is an impressive piece of silverware. Introduced in 1995, the trophy is made of sterling silver with gold detailing and features the signatures of Formula 1's world champions, stretching back to Giuseppe Farina in 1950.

So why wasn't it visible in Mexico City?

The answer lies in the divide between Formula 1 and its governing body, the FIA.

While F1, owned by Liberty Media, controls the commercial side of the championship, the FIA oversees its sporting and regulatory affairs. The world championship trophy falls under the FIA's jurisdiction -- Antonelli on Sunday officially became the FIA Formula 1 world champion - and its regulations stipulate that it must be presented at the governing body's annual gala.

Liberty Media has been keen to make more of the championship trophy. Sources have told ESPN discussions over a change this year did take place -- as they have for successive years now -- that the trophy be presented to Antonelli the moment he won it this year. However, as has also happened in previous seasons, it was agreed the FIA would stick with the convention of previous seasons and opt against doing anything radically different this time around.

- Antonelli makes F1 history as youngest world champion with maiden title

- Verstappen wins Mexico City GP for Red Bull; Antonelli seals historic title

- Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

The FIA has long argued that presenting the trophy at its gala is important to the occasion's prestige. The event celebrates champions from across motorsport, including rallying, endurance racing and karting, with the presence of Formula 1's world champion regarded as an important attraction for the younger winners.

There is also a sporting justification, as race results can be challenged or altered after the chequered flag, potentially changing the outcome of a championship. The FIA prefers to wait until those matters are settled before handing over its biggest prize.

That argument has some merit, although less so when Antonelli has wrapped up the championship with four races still to run. It rather falls apart altogether when considering what happens at every grand prix as it is the exact opposite of the practice the FIA puts forward in that instance. Individual race trophies are handed out immediately after the finish, despite those results also being subject to protests, penalties and subsequent disqualifications. If a result changes, the trophies simply change hands.

Look no further than Sunday's race in Mexico City for an example. Antonelli was clutching his third-place Mexico City Grand Prix trophy in his hands at different points during his celebratory moments on the podium and the ceremony which followed. That despite the fact a post-race penalty or protest could have moved him down the order after the fact -- it wouldn't have stopped him being champion, but it would have meant he should not have been on the podium. And yet, he did not have the world championship trophy in his hand for that exact same reason.

There is little reason why the championship should be treated differently to an individual race, especially when the current practice stops the trophy becoming a prize that champions can share with fans in the celebratory moments.

It seems a missed opportunity for a sport which has spent the past decade transforming the way it presents itself to the world. F1 has embraced new audiences, new technology and new ways of celebrating its biggest moments, yet its most prestigious prize remains tied to an awards dinner.

Antonelli will undoubtedly enjoy getting his hands on the trophy in Shanghai. But the moment he became world champion, surrounded by his Mercedes team and thousands of celebrating fans in Mexico City, has already passed and it is a moment Formula 1 cannot recreate.

stories.headline: Misiorowski, three other members of Brewers among MLB award finalists
stories.summary: Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski is among four members of the World Series champions who are finalists for baseball's biggest individual awards.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski is among four members of the World Series champions who are finalists for baseball's biggest individual awards.

Misiorowski, a heavy favorite to win the National League Cy Young Award, was one of the top three vote-getters in balloting for the prize by the Baseball Writers' Association of America at the conclusion of the regular season.

Finalists for all the major BBWAA awards were announced Monday night on MLB Network. Winners will be revealed next week.

Gold Glove second baseman Brice Turang is in the running for NL MVP, and Milwaukee skipper Pat Murphy could become the first to win three consecutive Manager of the Year awards. Brewers closer Trevor Megill is a finalist for NL Relief Pitcher of the Year, a new category this year in both leagues.

The awards finalists:

AL MVP: Houston slugger Yordan Alvarez is the favorite to win. Third baseman Junior Caminero from the American League champion Tampa Bay Rays and shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. of the Kansas City Royals are the other finalists.

NL MVP: Gold Glove center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs is expected to win after batting .280 with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases, becoming the seventh member of the 40-40 club. Turang and four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers are also finalists.

AL Cy Young: It's between Toronto right-hander Dylan Cease, Cleveland lefty Parker Messick and New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler. Messick's top-three finish as a rookie earns the Guardians an extra pick after the first round of the 2027 amateur draft.

NL Cy Young: Chris Sale of the Atlanta Braves and fellow left-hander Cristopher Sanchez from the Philadelphia Phillies join Misiorowski.

AL Rookie of the Year: Messick is also a candidate here, along with Detroit infielder Kevin McGonigle and Boston left-hander Payton Tolle.

NL Rookie of the Year: New York Mets right fielder Carson Benge is joined by Cincinnati Reds infielder Sal Stewart and St. Louis Cardinals second baseman JJ Wetherholt.

AL Relief Pitcher of the Year: The contenders are Tampa Bay closer Bryan Baker, Cleveland closer Cade Smith and Toronto closer Louis Varland.

NL Relief Pitcher of the Year: The other candidates besides Megill are Philadelphia closer Jhoan Duran and San Diego closer Mason Miller.

AL Manager of the Year: Kevin Cash from the Rays, Chad Tracy of the Boston Red Sox and Will Venable from the Chicago White Sox are in the running.

NL Manager of the Year: Murphy's challengers are Philadelphia's Don Mattingly and Atlanta's Walt Weiss.
